title: Serum protein gap adds modest albuminuria discrimination across two independently sampled NHANES cycles
abstract: A fixed model trained in NHANES2005–2006 (n=4081, 519 single-spot albuminuria cases) was evaluated without recalibration in independently sampled NHANES2009–2010 (n=5545, 597 cases). Adding total protein minus serum albumin to clinical/metabolic risk factors, serum creatinine and serum albumin increased AUC from 0.752342 to 0.765815. The difference was 0.013473, conditional paired95% interval [0.008155,0.018829], source/target-refit interval [0.006983,0.019668]. Log loss fell 0.295805→0.291207. This is a modest cross-sectional incremental-prediction result, not a new physiological measurement, persistent CKD diagnosis, clinical utility demonstration or non-NHANES validation.
